decision.question: layout_edge_problems' check 1 (text touching its box) flooded false positives when run literally per the brief: any text that fills a padded container naturally ends at the padding's inner edge (distance ~0 from the content box), which the brief's own parenthetical calls fine, not a bug. options: ship the literal per-side-content-box-distance rule as written

log.msg: KNOWN SCOPE LIMIT, documented rather than fixed: on every Doc-shelled page (tabs, doc-well, h1.doc-title), the title/well/tabs belong to an ANCESTOR Page instance (`.page.doc-page`, class `active-ancestor`), never to `.page.active-page` (the active LEAF, e.g. a doc-section tab's own content). Verified live on /framework/core/Page/doc/: active-page is `.page.doc-section.page--doc`, its own h1 is a generic `.page-title` (text 'loading', a loading placeholder), while the real `.doc-title`/`.doc-well`/tabs sit on the parent `.page.doc-page.page--Page.active-ancestor`. Since this task's brief explicitly scopes both checks to `.page.active-page` (the same scoping `links_on` already uses, to avoid picking up the sidebar/crumbs/dev-bar that repeat on every page), neither check can see a Doc-shell's own title/cost-line interaction — exactly the page TYPE the owner's original report was about. Decided to keep the brief's scoping as instructed rather than widen it to ancestors (widening would reintroduce the sidebar/crumbs noise links_on's own comment warns against, site-wide, and this task's budget does not cover redesigning that scope safely). What the checks DO catch, proven above: any ordinary (non-Doc-shell) page where a title and other content share the same `.page.active-page` — the much more common page shape on this site. Noted as a limitation in Server/doc/review.md's new line and left as a follow-up if the owner wants ancestor coverage.
